figures.caption: Figure 3 | Controllable image retrieval on clinically confusable differentials. a, Recall@1 on six visually confusable CT and chest-X-ray differential groups, where candidates share the same modality and anatomical region. Random indicates chance performance; CT-CLIP and PMC-CLIP are the strongest applicable CT and chest-X-ray baselines. b, Representative retrieval examples for pulmonary-artery enlargement versus hilar lymphadenopathy on CT studies.

Figure 1 | Overview of this study. a, Radiological comparison is formulated around temporal follow-up and reference-case reasoning. b, MedReCo uses an entity-conditioned visual representation to support both retrieval and vision–language generation. c, MedReCo-DB integrates multi-modal imaging data with entity-level clinical annotations. d, The benchmark includes both prior–current temporal comparisons and cross-case reference comparisons. e, Representative retrieval results evaluate entityconditioned reference matching. f, Representative VQA results evaluate entity-specific comparative reasoning.

Figure 6 | Ablation studies. a, Comparison between MoE-ViT and Shared-ViT for controllable image retrieval. Results are reported as Recall@1 (%) on the internal validation sets across all imaging modalities and three entity granularities. b, Comparison between the Full model and the InfoNCE-only variant for generative comparative interpretation. Results are reported as closed-ended comparative-interpretation accuracy (%) using the same modality and entity-granularity layout. Higher values indicate better performance. Error bars, 95% CI. Top-right value, dataset-level McNemar p (pooled across the three granularities). ***p < 0.001; **p < 0.01; *p < 0.05.

Figure 8 | Training framework of MedReCo (a) Image–text representation alignment. The vision encoder is first aligned with the text encoder using image–report pairs. (b) Text-guided contrastive pre-training. The aligned vision encoder is further optimized with text-guided contrastive learning to support controllable image retrieval. (c) Instruction tuning for comparative reasoning. Finally, the pre-trained vision encoder is adapted to the LLM through instruction tuning, enabling comparative interpretation with explanatory language.

Figure 7 | MedReCo dataset and benchmark overview. a, Data composition and benchmark splits across seven imaging modalities and eight source datasets spanning clinical centres in the USA, Turkey, Spain, and China. MedReCo comprises over 690,000 images from more than 160,000 patients; source datasets are assigned to internal validation or held-out external validation cohorts to evaluate cross-centre generalisability. b, Comparative data construction pipeline. Image-paired clinical reports are decomposed into structured, entity-specific descriptions at multiple granularities. For each image pair, entity-aware similarity is quantified using three clinical NLP metrics, and comparative VQAs are generated and carefully filtered to ensure clinical relevance and consistency. c, Representative entity-level coverage across modalities at three clinical granularities: anatomical structures, abnormal findings, and pathological conditions, curated per modality with radiologist review. d, Representative comparative VQA examples across modalities. Each image pair is annotated with both closed-ended multiple-choice and open-ended questions targeting modality-specific clinical entities, with key clinical terms highlighted by entity type.

Figure 5 | Generative comparative interpretation in longitudinal follow-up. a, Accuracy on same-patient prior–current generative comparative interpretation, analysed by abnormal finding and by radiologist-prioritized follow-up attribute. Statistical significance is denoted as *P<0.05, **P<0.01 and ***P<0.001. GGO, ground-glass opacity; Abd./Pelvic, abdominal/pelvic. b, Two representative longitudinal CT cases. The left case shows resolution of ground-glass opacity (GGO) previously seen around bilateral predominantly subpleural consolidation, whereas the right case shows newly developed bilateral centriacinar GGO in both lungs, especially in the upper lobes.

Figure 2 | Entity-conditioned reference-case retrieval performance. a, Internal-validation results across four imaging modalities and three entity levels: anatomical structures, abnormal findings and pathological conditions. Recall@1 is reported. Baselines are shown only for their intended modalities. Statistical significance is denoted as *P<0.05, **P<0.01 and ***P<0.001; n.s., not significant. b, Abnormal-finding subcategory analysis in CT and brain MR. Star markers denote MedReCo and circular markers denote baseline methods. All comparisons in this panel meet the significance threshold P<0.001. Abbreviations: ILD, interstitial lung disease; CHD, coronary heart disease; HTN, hypertension; Parench., parenchymal; IV/IC, intraventricular/intracisternal. c, External validation results on held-out chest-X-ray and CT cohorts. d, Cross-center retrieval from external reference archive.
